_comment: Codex CLI hooks adapter: the git-push safety gate + secret-guard.mjs, both PreToolUse. Verification status, updated 2026-07-25 via a direct fetch of https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (OpenAI's official Codex hooks reference, redirected from developers.openai.com/codex/hooks) -- schema-confirmed, still NOT tested against a live Codex CLI install (no configured model provider in this dev sandbox). What that fetch resolved, all previously open questions: (1) hooks are ENABLED BY DEFAULT (feature key `hooks`, `codex_hooks` a deprecated alias for the same flag; a third-party source claiming opt-in-required was checked directly against the primary docs and found wrong) -- no config.toml change needed to use this file. (2) `Bash` and `apply_patch` (file edits) both emit PreToolUse events, and BOTH scannable-content fields are the exact same JSON key -- `tool_input.command` -- confirmed directly, not guessed; secret-guard.mjs is now wired below using that confirmed field. (3) The stdin/stdout hook contract (`hookSpecificOutput.{hookEventName,permissionDecision,permissionDecisionReason}`) is byte-identical in shape to Claude Code's own -- Codex modeled its hooks system on it directly. Still genuinely open, disclosed rather than hidden: real GitHub issues (openai/codex#16732, #20204) report apply_patch hook events not firing consistently across all Codex CLI versions despite being documented as supported -- treat secret-guard.mjs as 'should fire per spec,' verify with a trivial known-bad edit on your own install before trusting it silently. Deliberately NOT included: the ExitPlanMode-matcher boardroom-checkpoint gate (Codex CLI has no plan-mode tool at all; it uses approval_policy instead -- nothing to gate here, not a missed port).

PreToolUse._matcher_comment: CONFIRMED via OpenAI's official Codex hooks docs: 'Bash' is a real, documented intercepted tool for PreToolUse/PostToolUse.

hooks._command_comment: Replace <PATH-TO-YOUR-INSTALLED-WINGMAN-PLUGIN> with wherever Claude Code's plugin marketplace installed Wingman on this machine (or a checked-out copy of the LabLaunchPad/Wingman repo). Reuses the real script unmodified -- see plugins/wingman/scripts/dod-pre-push-check.mjs, which already runs standalone with zero Claude Code involvement. Simpler and more robust than this hooks.json path: install it as a real git pre-push hook instead (item 3 of the harness-adapters README) -- that fires under any harness, including this one, with no Codex-specific wiring at all.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: checking Boardroom verdict, tests, and threat register before allowing a git push

hooks._command_comment: Ported from plugins/wingman/hooks/secret-guard.mjs -- blocks destructive commands and real secret patterns before they run. Real, tested (schema-verified via a synthetic stdin/stdout round-trip, not just written and assumed), not just written and assumed.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning for destructive commands and secret patterns

PreToolUse._matcher_comment: CONFIRMED via the same official docs: file edits performed through apply_patch emit PreToolUse events, with the patch/diff text in tool_input.command -- the same field name Bash uses, not a separate content/new_string field like Claude Code's Write/Edit.

hooks._command_comment: Same script as the Bash matcher above -- it reads tool_input.command regardless of tool_name, so one script covers both matchers.
hooks.statusMessage: Wingman: scanning file edit for secret patterns
